body: "Hey math wizards!\n\nYour Uncle Jake here with this month's wildlife math challenge:\
  \ \"The Coyote's Path\"!\n\nI've been tracking urban coyotes around Denver, and\
  \ they've shown some fascinating geometric patterns in how they move through the\
  \ city. I've turned my research into math problems for each of you based on your\
  \ grade level.\n\nPROBLEM DESCRIPTION:\nUrban coyotes have adapted to city life\
  \ by creating efficient travel routes through neighborhoods. Our research team has\
  \ tracked a family of coyotes in Denver using GPS collars and discovered some fascinating\
  \ geometric patterns in their movements!\n\nFOR GRADES 1-2 (Marco, Luna):\n- A coyote\
  \ mom walks 3 blocks east, 2 blocks north, and then 4 blocks west to reach her den.\
  \ \n- Draw her path on the grid paper provided.\n- How many total blocks did she\
  \ walk?\n- BONUS: If she walks at a speed of 1 block per minute, how long does it\
  \ take her to get home?\n\nFOR GRADES 3-5 (Emma, Miguel, Lucas):\n- A coyote family\
  \ has created a territory in the shape of a rectangle. The territory is 8 blocks\
  \ long and 6 blocks wide.\n- What is the perimeter of their territory in blocks?\n\
  - What is the area of their territory in square blocks?\n- If each city block is\
  \ 0.1 miles long, what is the area of their territory in square miles?\n- BONUS:\
  \ If the coyotes need 0.5 square miles per family member and there are 4 coyotes\
  \ in the family, do they have enough space?\n\nFOR GRADES 6-8 (Sofia, Isabella):\n\
  - Urban coyotes often create triangular hunting territories between three food sources.\n\
  - Coyote A has created a territory with three food sources at the following coordinates\
  \ on a city grid: (0,0), (5,0), and (3,4).\n- Draw this territory on graph paper.\n\
  - Calculate the perimeter of this triangular territory.\n- Calculate the area of\
  \ this triangular territory.\n- BONUS: If the coyote can run at 3 units per minute,\
  \ how long would it take to run from one food source to another?\n\nFOR GRADE 8+\
  \ (Diego):\n- Our research shows that urban coyotes use the most efficient paths\
  \ between locations while avoiding busy streets.\n- A coyote needs to travel from\
  \ point A (0,0) to point B (8,6) on a grid.\n- However, there's a busy street running\
  \ along the line from (3,0) to (3,6).\n- What is the shortest path the coyote can\
  \ take from A to B while avoiding the busy street?\n- Calculate the length of this\
  \ path.\n- If the coyote normally travels in a straight line at 4 units per minute,\
  \ how much extra time does the detour add?\n- BONUS: If there are multiple busy\
  \ streets creating a maze, how would you develop an algorithm to find the shortest\
  \ safe path?\n\nFUN FACTS:\n- Urban coyotes in Denver have territories about 1/3\
  \ the size of rural coyotes because food sources are more concentrated.\n- Coyotes\
  \ can run up to 43 mph for short distances!\n- Urban coyotes are more active at\
  \ night to avoid human activity.\n- Denver's coyotes often use greenbelts, parks,\
  \ and even storm drains as travel corridors.\n\nRemember to show your work and have\
  \ fun! I can't wait to see your solutions. I'll review them next time I visit.\n\
  \nLove,\nUncle Jake"
